newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Clinics deal injects life into Netcare.
newsitem.headline: Clinics deal injects life into Netcare.

text.p: Shares in South African hospital management company Netcare Ltd jumped in early Monday trade after it announced at the weekend it had acquired a controlling interest in Clinic Holdings Limited (Clinics).
By 0845 GMT, the counter had rallied 14 cents or seven percent to a four-week high of 214 cents after some 1.68 million shares worth 3.57 million rand had changed hands.
"It's because of the deal with Clinics," a trader said.
The company announced at the weekend it would acquire a controlling stake in Clinics for 920 million rand -- making Netcare the largest hospital group in South Africa.

Dealers said that there had been broad-based institutional interest in the share and expected more to follow. "Interest in the share is coming from all institutions...there are a few big orders in the market," one said.
An analyst said that while details of the deal were sketchy, it would have positive implications for the company.
"All the details of the transaction are not available yet, there is another cautionary and rights issues coming from Netcare and Clinics," the analyst said.
"But generally given the positive shareholder implications, the critical mass that the new deal will give them...it looks positive."
The companies said in a joint statement that talks about further acquisitions and transactions were at an advanced stage and could have an effect on the companies' share prices.
Clinics shares were last up 10 cents at 500 cents.
